title: Scheme-test category of quasi-coherent smooth-atlas module descent data
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal X$ be a category over $\mathit{Sch}/S$, and let $a:h_U\to\mathcal X$ be a functor over the base, with discrete representable fibred groupoids as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Module sheaves use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and quasi-coherence uses the local-presentation predicate of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site], use the regular-function structure sheaf obtained by restricting the sheaf of scheme global sections to the slice over $U$. Apply the canonical coefficient ULift of [def-pur-cochain-coefficient-universe-transport] into the ambient universe containing schemes and both universes of $\mathcal X$, as for [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Restriction along the forgetful functor from the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] to the big fppf site is continuous. Its module restriction has the tensor-extension left adjoint $A_U$ of [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-pullback-exists-universes], with its adjunction unit retained. The etale structure rings are the restriction of these regular-function rings. For an etale quasi-coherent module $M$ write $A_U(M)(T,f)$ for the sections of this associated big-site module at $f:T\to U$.

Define the category of atlas module descent data as follows. An object is a quasi-coherent module $M$ on $U_{et}$ and, for every $S$-scheme $T$, maps $f,g:T\to U$, and vertical isomorphism $q:a(g)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(f)$ over $1_T$, an additive isomorphism $\delta_q:A_U(M)(T,f)\to A_U(M)(T,g)$. It is linear for the same regular functions on $T$, natural under all test maps $h:T'\to T$ and squares $q'\,a(h,f)=a(h,g)\,q$, equal to the identity when $f=g$ and $q=1$, and satisfies $\delta_r\delta_q=\delta_{q\circ r}$ for composable vertical isomorphisms. This is the inverse-arrow convention for the relation $U\times_{\mathcal X}U$, which is interpreted on scheme tests and need not be a scheme. Morphisms are all module maps $b:M\to N$ satisfying $\delta_N A_U(b)_f=A_U(b)_g\delta_M$ on every such test. Identities and composition are those of module maps; the forgetful functor retains $M$ and $b$.
